nodes.description: Progressive degeneration resembling a cone-rod dystrophy, with atrophy beginning at the posterior pole and spreading peripherally, causing loss of central and colour vision. Onset and course vary widely, even within one family. Its cause is unresolved. Two models are recorded: a consequence of chronic intraocular inflammation (inflammation_model) and a ciliary defect (ciliopathy_model). Degeneration can progress after inflammation is controlled, so it is probably not purely inflammatory.

nodes.description: Wild-type ALPK1 is a cytosolic pattern-recognition receptor that is activated when bacterial ADP-heptose binds its N-terminal domain. The ROSAH mutants can also be activated by host nucleotide sugars (UDP-mannose, ADP-ribose, cyclic ADP-ribose), so the kinase signals without infection. The authors propose this loss of specificity as the basis of the disease.
